title: Recombinant DNA from gene cloning through risk governance to industrial biotechnology
pressure: Methods to cut/ligate DNA and plasmids could propagate recombinant molecules, opening new capability with uncertain biohazards.
preExistingWorldModel: Molecular genetics and restriction enzymes existed; risk magnitude for cross-species recombinant organisms was not known.
observationsAndInstruments: Cohen/Boyer demonstrated recombinant plasmid cloning in 1973.
Scientists publicly raised hazard concerns and deferred selected experiments.
Asilomar developed risk-contingent safeguards rather than a permanent ban.
NIH guidelines formalized containment and responsibilities.
Recombinant DNA became an industrial biotech platform including human proteins.
decisiveTests: contain plausible harms enough to permit research under uncertainty
technicalOrScientificTransition: A new manipulation method changed the risk surface; bounded experimentation and institutional rules co-evolved with the research platform rather than merely blocking it.
rivalsAndFailures: A temporary pause reduced immediate freedom but preserved a path to continued research.
Gene cloning did not itself establish product safety or industrial manufacturing.
Commercialization introduced ownership/authority questions separate from laboratory biosafety.
diffusionAndScaling: Diffusion depended on complements, cost/yield/standards and institutional adoption; the nominal breakthrough date did not equal broad effective use.
standardsAndInstitutions: Laboratories, firms, standard bodies, regulators, users and infrastructure operators owned different parts of evidence, implementation and consequence.
externalitiesAndCorrections: Lifecycle harms and authority changes are preserved where evidenced rather than inferred from local technical success.
secondOrderEffects: A new manipulation method changed the risk surface; bounded experimentation and institutional rules co-evolved with the research platform rather than merely blocking it.
sourceNativeSummary: A new manipulation method changed the risk surface; bounded experimentation and institutional rules co-evolved with the research platform rather than merely blocking it.
unresolvedHistoricalQuestions: Which complement most constrained diffusion at each lifecycle phase?
